sections.h2: Scott County property tax at a glance
sections.html:
Scott County is small, and property tax questions land on a handful of courthouse desks in Winchester, the county seat, at 35 East Market Street. The 2020 census counted 4,949 people, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 4,866, down 4.1%. The county has 2,377 housing units, and owners hold 79.0% of occupied homes.

The typical owner-reported home value is $96,400, and the middle renter pays $689 a month gross. With values at that level, a small change in condition or tax status can swing how fast a house sells, so it pays to know your bill and your paperwork before you list.

sections.h2: Which offices handle assessments, bills and records?
sections.html:
Three offices cover most property tax questions: the Assessor, the Treasurer and the County Clerk. Each has its own page at scottcoil.gov, and each does a separate job in the yearly cycle.

  • The Assessor (Supervisor of Assessments) applies exemptions, maintains the parcel numbers and map files, sends assessment notices, runs the appeal process and certifies the roll to the County Clerk. Call 217-742-5751 or write to assessor@scottcoil.gov.
  • The Treasurer collects real estate and mobile home taxes, keeps the revenue records, pays out the money to taxing bodies and answers parcel questions.
  • The County Clerk works with the Treasurer on the yearly delinquent tax sale. The county site also has property record and fee schedule pages for deed and record requests.

The assessor's fee list was updated on April 27, 2026. A property record card costs $1.00, copies are $0.50 per page, a letter-size printed aerial map is $10.00 and an emailed PDF aerial map is $5.00. Pull the record card before you list. It shows the house characteristics the assessment rests on, and a wrong square footage or bedroom count is easy to fix at this stage.

sections.h2: Due dates and how bills work
sections.html:
The Treasurer posts payment dates at the top of its page each year. Bills go out in early summer and are payable in two installments, one in July and one in September. In 2026 the bills were mailed June 8, with installments due July 17 and September 18. Call the Treasurer for the schedule on your next bill.

Illinois bills a year behind, so taxes for one year are billed and collected the next. A house sold in autumn still has a bill coming that covers the year the seller owned it, and the closing statement has to deal with that. Mobile home taxes go through the same office on their own bills.

sections.h2: Exemptions that lower a Scott County bill
sections.html:
Each exemption reduces the equalized assessed value that the rate is applied to. Apply through the Chief County Assessment Office, which takes both first applications and renewals. Ask whether the previous owner's exemption carries over or needs a new filing in your name.

Exemptions on the Scott County exemptions page
ExemptionBenefitForm or proof
General homesteadRise in assessed value over the 1977 figure, up to $6,000Owner-occupied residence
Senior citizens assessment freezeHolds the assessed value; income ceiling rises starting with the 2026 yearFederal return with every schedule
Returning service members$5,000 off for two straight tax yearsForm PTAX-341
Persons with disabilities$2,000 off each yearYearly Form PTAX-343-R
Disabled service members, standard$2,500 at a 30% to 50% rating, $5,000 at 50% to 70%, full exemption at 70% or moreTotal value under $250,000
Specially adapted housingAs much as $100,000 off assessed valueService-connected disability
Homestead improvementNew rooms, remodels and rebuilds shielded for four years, up to $75,000 fair cash value ($25,000 assessed)Permit and completed work

The senior freeze ceiling comes from Public Act 104-0452, signed December 12, 2025. Once 2028 is past, the ceiling holds at $79,000 unless lawmakers act again.

The window is short. Section 16-55(d) of the Property Tax Code gives an owner 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list to get a written complaint to the Board of Review. A mailed complaint counts from its postmark, and a courier package from the shipper's label, so keep the receipt.

The board is told to weigh compulsory sales, including ones the owner submits, when they share the property's features and condition. Start with the Assessor's record card and find out what drove the new value. Then collect recent sales of similar Scott County houses. An owner who loses can carry the dispute to the Property Tax Appeal Board. Only the assessed value is in play, because the taxing districts set the rates.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Each year the Treasurer, with help from the County Clerk, sells off delinquent real estate taxes, delinquent mobile home taxes and unpaid special assessments. A parcel left unpaid can end up in that sale.

Call the Treasurer's Office for the balance on the parcel, the sale date and any earlier year left open. The County Clerk explains redemption steps and costs, so ask for the balance in writing. Settle any open year before you list, since the buyer's title search will turn up the same thing.

An unpaid bill does not block a sale, but the buyer will expect it cleared by closing. The closing agent usually gets the balance from the Treasurer, pays it out of the seller's share and then records the deed.

  • Section 31-10 sets the state transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 block of stated value. A transfer declaration (PTAX-203, or MyDec online) goes in with the deed.
  • Phone the County Clerk before closing day about recording fees and any county stamp.
  • Of the county's 2,388 housing units in the 2020 count, 12.0% were vacant, so buyers have plenty of choices and tend to push on price when a file looks messy.

Owners who inherited a house, cannot fund repairs or have fallen behind on taxes have three paths: a listing, a private deal or a sale to a buyer who takes the house in its present state. The third path skips repair work, though the tax payoff is still settled at closing.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
A few errands in Winchester make a Scott County sale smoother. Start with the Assessor's record card for your parcel and check the square footage and room count. Next, ask the Treasurer for a written balance and confirm that no earlier year is open. Then ask the Assessor which exemptions are on the parcel today, because a buyer's lender will see them on the bill.

Bring your parcel number and a photo ID, and expect to pay the small fees above for copies. If an addition or remodel went in during your ownership, find the permit paperwork, since the improvement exemption and the record card both depend on it.

faqs.q: Where is the Scott County courthouse?
faqs.a: The county seat is Winchester, at 35 East Market Street. The Treasurer, Assessor and County Clerk each have their own page at scottcoil.gov.

faqs.q: When are Scott County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in early summer, with two installments in July and September. In 2026 they were due July 17 and September 18. The Treasurer's Office can give the next set of dates.

faqs.q: How much is the general homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The maximum is $6,000, measured against the 1977 equalized assessed value, for counties outside the Cook County area.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file an assessment complaint?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days from publication of the assessment list. Put the complaint in writing, send it to the Board of Review and keep the postmark or tracking label.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Scott County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent gets the balance from the Treasurer and pays it from the seller's share, so the buyer does not inherit the debt.
